title: Annual flow correction left no clear recession change in 158-163 south-east Australian catchments in 2010-2021
abstract: We test whether a constant flow amplitude can describe both annual runoff loss and daily recession change in south-east Australia. We undo each published annual weather-adjusted retention in CAMELS-AUS v2.03 daily flow, then match flow, season and dry-spell age on common days. In 158 catchments in 2010-2021, the raw recession change was -3.3% [-9.0, +2.9] and the corrected change was +2.4% [-4.1, +10.9]. Limits are conditional 95% spatial intervals. The test links annual fit statistics to raw daily observations. It uses established recession scaling algebra. The annual ratio is not a measured daily gain; fitted-model, temporal and measurement uncertainty are not included. Earlier-period and second-rain-product checks are supplied. This tests a constant-amplitude description and does not identify the physical cause of runoff loss. Code, hashes, source rights, all draws, aggregate statistics, a figure and a synthetic audit are included.
